records.source_claim: The right-module definition x(ab)=(xa)b is said to be equivalent to a unital algebra homomorphism Phi:A->L(V).
records.adjudication: With standard operator composition, a right action yields Phi(ab)=Phi(b)Phi(a), so Phi is an antihomomorphism A->L(V), equivalently a homomorphism A^op->L(V).
records.proof_witness: For Phi(a)x=xa, module associativity gives Phi(ab)x=x(ab)=(xa)b=Phi(b)Phi(a)x.
records.counterexample: For A=M_2(C) acting on V=A on the right, R_a R_b=R_{ba}; with a=E_12 and b=E_21, ab=E_11 differs from ba=E_22.
records.reader_resolution: The admitted Erdman translation remains byte-identical; the separately authored solution states the inconsistency and proves the corrected equivalence.
